issues.description: Duplicate 'transcriber_error' entry in the error-type tuple reveals wrong data structure.
issues.detail: The membership tuple lists 'transcriber_error' twice — a defect a set literal would have caught at write-time. The fourteen error strings inlined in an elif are data masquerading as control flow. Lift them to a module-level frozenset (ERROR_MESSAGE_TYPES); the duplicate disappears, the membership test becomes self-evident, and new error codes become a one-line data edit.

issues.description: Removing the outer try/except changes the receive-loop contract without documenting it.
issues.detail: The old code swallowed exceptions and returned normally, defeating the reconnect loop — the fix is correct. But the new contract ('returns iff stream ended cleanly; raises on transport error') must be written into the docstring so future edits do not re-introduce the swallow. The invariant proving termination on permanent failure is not stated.

issues.description: Collapsed 'Error:' prefix weakens push_error's observable postcondition.
issues.detail: The previous code distinguished 'Auth error:' and 'Quota exceeded:' prefixes; the new unified branch drops both per-type logging and typed prefixes, so observers can no longer distinguish error class without re-parsing. Either pass message_type as a structured field, restore typed prefixes, or at minimum restore a logger.error line including message_type for operability.

issues.description: Inner try/except Exception still masks transport errors and conflates failure modes.
issues.detail: The remaining bare 'except Exception' inside the async-for catches transport-level exceptions raised mid-iteration alongside JSON/handler errors, partially undermining the 'raise on disconnect' contract this PR establishes. Narrow the except to handler-domain exceptions, or re-raise after logging if the exception did not originate from _process_response.

issues.description: Fallback error string fabricates 'Unknown error' instead of using typed event fields.
issues.detail: data.get('error', f'Unknown error - {message_type}') assumes every one of the fourteen message types carries an 'error' field. The ElevenLabs schema likely uses different field names per type (e.g., 'reason', 'message'). Most error frames will read 'Unknown error - rate_limited' even when a useful payload is present. Enumerate the per-type field shapes.

changelog/3233.fixed.md lacks a terminating newline. Trivial, but the convention across the changelog directory is part of the implicit contract for downstream release-notes concatenation tooling. Add the newline.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR fixes a real bug: the outer try/except in the receive loop was swallowing disconnect exceptions and defeating the websocket reconnect loop, so collapsing to a single async-for is correctly shaped. Consensus concerns center on the broadened error-type handling: the fourteen-element inline tuple is the wrong data structure (already proven by a duplicate 'transcriber_error' entry) and should be lifted to a named frozenset. The unified 'Error:' prefix weakens push_error's observable postcondition relative to the prior typed prefixes, and the new receive-loop contract ('raises on transport error') needs to be documented so future edits do not re-introduce the swallow. Minor hygiene: trailing newline on the changelog, narrower inner except, and a better fallback than the fabricated 'Unknown error' string.
